holdings.thesis: HOLD: no negative catalyst; incremental positives since 9/16 -- Nvidia, Google, and Emerald AI launched an alliance for flexible AI data-center power management, and Berkshire Hathaway's latest 13-F showed an 83% QoQ increase to its Alphabet stake, now Berkshire's third-largest equity position. A Pixel firmware bug (CVE-2026-58704) exploited in limited targeted attacks was already patched -- narrow scope, not a broad business risk. Position ~15.5%, a touch over the nominal 15% target but within the trim tolerance band -- watch for sizing drift, no action needed today.

TRIMMED today: thesis intact; the persistent earnings-decline flag continues to reflect deliberate AI-feature reinvestment (folding former "Max" features into the base Super tier), not demand weakness. New item to note: sell-side sentiment is now more mixed than any other holding (6 buy vs. 2 sell, average 12-month PT ~$134.29 is actually below the current ~$147 price) -- a first for this position, worth watching but not a fresh negative catalyst on its own. Separately, adding MOD today pushed the Technology sector to 30.16% of the portfolio, over the 30% sector_max_pct cap -- trimmed 0.0983 shares (~$14.46) from DUOL, the largest Tech position, to bring the sector back to ~29.8%. This is a pure sizing rebalance, not a change of view; fundamentals-driven thesis unchanged.

HOLD: AWS confirmed this week that data/resources hosted solely in its Bahrain region cannot be recovered (an escalation in language from the earlier "cannot restore" framing) following March's Iran-linked strike damage -- still a regional reliability issue, not a broad US AWS outage, with no disclosed customer or revenue impact. Also monitoring pre-existing FTC/22-state litigation alleging ad-pricing practices that may have cost advertisers up to $20B -- a known regulatory overhang, not a new escalation. Thesis otherwise intact.

HOLD: incrementally positive -- Exxon is reportedly nearing a deal for access to Venezuela's Orinoco Belt (50B+ barrels of reserves, reported 9/16-17), and management raised its LNG sales target to 50M tons by 2030 on rising global demand; Exxon is also lined up for new US-Vietnam energy/industrial agreements. Thesis (strong Q2 earnings, capital discipline, Angola Block 15 discovery) strengthened.

HOLD: second review of the same stop-loss breach trimmed yesterday (-25.3% vs. cost basis, price ~$241.49, essentially flat/slightly improved vs. -25.9% at the trim). No fresh VRT-specific catalyst -- today's broader softness ties to the Fed's 25bp rate hike (first since 2023) pushing the 10-year yield above 5%, a market-wide rate headwind rather than a company-specific issue. No new earnings miss, guidance cut, or litigation escalation found beyond the already-known securities-disclosure investigation and Massachusetts permitting overhang. Already de-risked 30% yesterday specifically for this breach and sell-side remains heavily bullish (83% buy-rated, ~$341 avg PT) -- holding the remainder without a further trim.

HOLD: positive -- Wolfe Research upgraded Affirm to Outperform with a $90 PT (vs. ~$70 price) on 9/16, citing strong Q4 results. Thesis (36% GMV growth, Affirm Card scaling, the 5-year Amazon renewal) intact and reinforced.

HOLD: seventh consecutive stop-loss review (-37.8% vs. cost basis, price ~$168.25). No new company-specific negative catalyst since 9/16; sell-side remains Strong Buy (19 analysts, consensus PT ~$281, ~73% implied upside), and FY27 guidance still implies 85%+ revenue growth with optical revenue on track to exceed $600M. Position is already a de-risked ~5.5% stub after three prior trims -- holding.
HOLD: no material negative news -- shares traded in a normal $227-237 range with some reported strength tied to CEO Olivier Pomel commentary. AI-observability demand thesis unchanged.

HOLD: positive -- Berenberg upgraded Lilly from Hold to Buy on 9/15, raising its PT from $1,220 to $1,400 on strong ROI and obesity-market growth; consensus PT now ~$1,392.50 (~22% implied upside). New TuneLab drug-discovery partnerships with Ginkgo Bioworks and Twist Bioscience announced 9/16. Obesity-franchise thesis intact and reinforced.

HOLD, still flagging sentiment risk: analysts remained "conflicted" on CAT alongside other AI-infrastructure-linked industrial names (BE, PWR) through 9/14-16 on AI-data-center-capex-slowdown concerns -- the same overhang already noted, no new escalation. $72B backlog and core industrial/Power & Energy thesis unchanged.
HOLD: no new company-specific news since the Citizens Bank litigation disclosure already reflected in thesis -- continuing to monitor that overhang. Core digital-bank/fintech thesis unchanged.

HOLD: positive -- IonQ research was recognized with four Best Paper Awards at IEEE Quantum Week 2026, reinforcing its technology-leadership positioning. No news affecting the raised FY26 guidance or the SkyWater-driven thesis. Holding the modest ~2.2% position.

HOLD, flagging a new execution-risk item on day two: AST SpaceMobile shifted its 45-satellites-in-orbit target from year-end 2026 to early 2027 -- no formal delay announced for BlueBirds 14-16, but the gap versus prior messaging is drawing investor scrutiny (Stocktwits sentiment stayed bearish). COO and CTO also filed proposed sales of ~52,000 shares (~$3.06M combined). This is exactly the "expensive, tightly-timed deployment" execution risk flagged at entry yesterday -- not thesis-breaking yet on a still-small ~2.1% position (+5.8% vs. cost basis), but worth close monitoring given how early this is in the holding period.

HOLD: mixed but net-neutral post-earnings analyst moves -- Jefferies trimmed its PT to $204 from $229 (kept Buy) while JPMorgan raised its PT to $210 from $200 (kept Overweight); both remain bullish. Record $1.5B backlog and the 9/9 Q1 FY27 beat remain the operative thesis, position +16% vs. cost basis.
HOLD: no new ticker-specific news found since 9/14-15. Thesis (incoming-CEO Paul Gu insider purchase, AI-underwriting) unchanged.

HOLD: eighth consecutive stop-loss review (-28.2% vs. cost basis, price ~$56.98). Mildly positive governance update -- the board added Admiral Michael Rogers (former NSA Director and US Cyber Command Commander) on 9/16, a credibility-supportive addition during the pending CEO transition (Singhal to CEO effective 9/30). No new negative catalyst; 58% YoY revenue growth and 40%+ FY guidance remain reaffirmed. Holding the remaining ~1.4% stub through the transition.

BUY: Modine Manufacturing sourced from the 9/8 weekly theme screen (AI data-center liquid-cooling/thermal management). FY26 net sales +23% YoY to $3.2B, driven by a 90% increase in data-center cooling revenue, and the company signed a new long-term agreement this week to supply over $4B in cooling products through 2029 -- multi-year revenue visibility. Forward P/E 16.8 with 28% revenue growth and 44% earnings growth is a reasonable growth-at-a-reasonable-price setup versus richer AI-infra peers (e.g. RKLB's ~1,489x forward P/E, screened but passed on for this reason). Opportunity-tier (market cap ~$9.8B, just under the $10B threshold); sized to the full remaining opportunity-bucket room (~$23, bucket already ~19.4% of its 20% cap) rather than a full position, funded by available cash above the 2% buffer floor. Note: company announced a 9/10 corporate name change to Modexus Solutions, effective date TBD -- ticker unaffected for now.

AST SpaceMobile sourced from the 9/8 weekly theme screen (direct-to-cell satellite connectivity). Shifting from proof-of-concept to commercial activation: BlueBird 11-13 satellites deployed, new New Zealand gateway opened, deepening carrier integration (Vodafone/Orange/Telefonica/Deutsche Telekom via a gateway JV) and US Mobile preparing a direct-to-cell launch. 2026 revenue guided to $150-200M (vs. a near-zero prior-year base, which drove the quantitative screen's outsized revenue-growth score), backed by a $1.3B backlog and over $3.7B cash funding the buildout. Key risk is execution on an expensive, tightly-timed deployment (implied ~165%/yr revenue growth needed through 2029), but the bull case is still considered intact by sell-side (~$78 fair-value estimate vs. ~$59.27 entry). Not opportunity-tier (~$23B market cap). Sized to the remaining Technology sector-cap room (~$81.65, sector already ~28% of portfolio) rather than a full position; funded by today's VRT trim proceeds.

First-ever stop-loss breach for VRT (-25.9% vs. cost basis at review), but unlike CRDO/INOD's chronic pattern this reads as a fresh, macro-beta-driven crossing -- Monday's broad AI-slowdown selloff hit Vertiv's ~2x-beta shares hard, and the stock was already recovering (~$234 on 9/15 toward ~$240 on 9/16). No earnings miss, guidance cut, or litigation; Q2 organic-growth guidance was actually raised to a 20-22% CAGR target through 2030, and sell-side remains heavily bullish (83% buy-rated, ~$341 average PT, GLJ upgrade to Buy $381). Trimming 30% to de-risk specifically because the 9/9 $1.45B UtilityInnovation Group acquisition still has undisclosed target financials and the Massachusetts data-center permitting order remains an unresolved overhang layered on top of the high beta -- not a full exit since there is no thesis-breaking catalyst.

AeroVironment reported Q1 FY27 results today (9/9): adjusted EPS $0.59 vs. $0.22 est., revenue $480.5M vs. $467.9M est., and a record funded backlog of $1.5B (+37% YoY). Two new contract wins landed this same week: a ~$500M Titan/JIATF-401 award and a ~$500M LOCUST counter-UAS (E-HEL) Army contract. Shares +4% on the print. Drone/robotics defense-tech pure-play sourced from the 9/1 theme screen; opportunity-tier small-cap ($7.2B market cap). Funded by today's AGX sale proceeds.

Shares fell ~8.2% to ~$401 on the news. Combined with an already-breached stop-loss (-34.6% vs. cost basis, the second consecutive stop-loss review) and the position already being small after two prior trims, exiting the remaining stub rather than holding through a fresh bearish catalyst.
